A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AReaL research work. All 27 pages, including figures, tables, equations, the checklist, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v4 reports original AReaL training and benchmark results, throughput measurements, scaling experiments, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results in renumbered Section 7 and Appendix C, including the additional architecture and staleness experiments.

M1.justification: The asynchronous architecture, interruptible generation, staleness control, decoupled PPO objective, and dynamic batching algorithm remain unchanged. Their sections are renumbered without modifying the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DeepScaleR and DeepCoder training data and retain evaluation on AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, MATH500, LiveCodeBench, Codeforces, and CodeContests. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including verl comparisons associated with DeepScaleR and DeepCoder, synchronous AReaL, and the configurations compared in the ablations.

E3.justification: The experimental setup, Table 1 settings, Table 3 hyperparameters, and appendix protocols are unchanged. Model sizes, GPU allocations, training budgets, context lengths, staleness settings, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical decoupled-objective and staleness ablations, dynamic batching and interruptible-generation studies, and Appendix C analyses of model architectures, small GPU setups, and RLOO.

E5.justification: Appendix A and Table 3 retain random seed 1. Both checklists report single-trial large-scale experiments without error bars because of computational expense. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Result entries in Tables 1–2 and 4–8 and plots in Figures 4–6 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains AReaL scores of 42.2 and 63.1 on AIME24 and 58.1 and 61.0 on LiveCodeBench.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(5), Proposition 1, and its Appendix D proof retain the same content. Differences in equation placement and section references do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning fully asynchronous RL, training efficiency, scalability, and matched or improved task performance.

C2.justification: Explanations of staleness, PPO stability, throughput bottlenecks, and generalization are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning device allocation and evaluation restricted to single-step math and coding tasks.

D1.justification: Software versions, hardware descriptions, implementation details, hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged in the implementation section and Appendices A–B. Updated section references add no technical disclosures.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and positioning relative to prior systems are unchanged. The corrected Related Work heading introduces no additional literature discussion.

P1.justification: v5 replaces the malformed 'sectionRelated Work' text with numbered Section 2. Subsequent sections, subsections, and cross-references are renumbered accordingly, and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The prose and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Proper heading typography and spacing produce limited reflow on pages 2–6, changing paragraph breaks and the placement of some material. Figure and table content, designs, and captions remain unchanged; appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v5 fixes the visibly malformed Related Work heading on page 2 and establishes a proper numbered section with corresponding reference updates. This modestly improves readability and presentation. The methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, proof, and limitations remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited.
